steps.say: Start with an empty map. It will hold every value to the left of j.
j = 0, x = 5. The map holds nums[:0]: every value to the left of j.
need = 7 − 5 = 2. A partner for x must have this value.
2 is not in the map, so no i < 0 pairs with x. One lookup ruled out all of column 0.
Store 5 → 0. The map now holds nums[:1], ready for j = 1.
j = 1, x = 8. The map holds nums[:1]: every value to the left of j.
need = 7 − 8 = -1. A partner for x must have this value.
-1 is not in the map, so no i < 1 pairs with x. One lookup ruled out all of column 1.
Store 8 → 1. The map now holds nums[:2], ready for j = 2.
j = 2, x = 1. The map holds nums[:2]: every value to the left of j.
need = 7 − 1 = 6. A partner for x must have this value.
6 is not in the map, so no i < 2 pairs with x. One lookup ruled out all of column 2.
Store 1 → 2. The map now holds nums[:3], ready for j = 3.
j = 3, x = 9. The map holds nums[:3]: every value to the left of j.
need = 7 − 9 = -2. A partner for x must have this value.
-2 is not in the map, so no i < 3 pairs with x. One lookup ruled out all of column 3.
Store 9 → 3. The map now holds nums[:4], ready for j = 4.
j = 4, x = 4. The map holds nums[:4]: every value to the left of j.

fade.q: Fill the map before stepping on: type it as value:index pairs, e.g. 5:0, 8:1

steps.say: need = 7 − 4 = 3. A partner for x must have this value.
3 is not in the map, so no i < 4 pairs with x. One lookup ruled out all of column 4.

predict.q: need = 3, and 3 is in nums. Is 3 in the map right now?
predict.why: 3 sits at index 5, to the right of j = 4. The map only holds nums[:4]. The pair is found when j reaches 3's index instead.

j = 5, x = 3. The map holds nums[:5]: every value to the left of j.
need = 7 − 3 = 4. A partner for x must have this value.
4 is in the map at index 4. One lookup answered all of column 5.

predict.q: need = 4. Is 4 in the map, and at which index?

steps.say: Return [seen[4], j] = [4, 5].
Returned [4, 5]: nums[4] + nums[5] = 7.

predict.why: The check runs before the insert, so x can't pair with itself. Swap lines 5–6 and line 7 and [3] with target 6 would wrongly return [0, 0].

presets.label: group_anagrams([eat, tea, tan, ate, nat, bat])

steps.say: Empty map. Each key will be a word's letters in sorted order.
Next word: "eat".
Sort the letters of "eat": key = "aet".
"aet" is not in the map yet: a new group.
Open an empty group under "aet".
Append "eat" to group "aet".
Next word: "tea".
Sort the letters of "tea": key = "aet".
"aet" is already in the map: "tea" joins that group without being compared with any word.
Append "tea" to group "aet".
Next word: "tan".
Sort the letters of "tan": key = "ant".
"ant" is not in the map yet: a new group.
Open an empty group under "ant".
Append "tan" to group "ant".
Next word: "ate".
Sort the letters of "ate": key = "aet".
"aet" is already in the map: "ate" joins that group without being compared with any word.

predict.q: key for "ate" is "aet". Is it already in the map?

steps.say: Append "ate" to group "aet".
Next word: "nat".
Sort the letters of "nat": key = "ant".
"ant" is already in the map: "nat" joins that group without being compared with any word.
Append "nat" to group "ant".
Next word: "bat".
Sort the letters of "bat": key = "abt".
"abt" is not in the map yet: a new group.

predict.q: key for "bat" is "abt". Is it already in the map?

steps.say: Open an empty group under "abt".
Append "bat" to group "abt".
No words left: the loop ends.
Return the 3 groups as a list of lists.
